Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Pakistan's reply. Harmanpreet Kaur leads her troops out onto the park. It will be the left-hand, right-hand combination of Muneeba Ali and Gull Feroza to open the innings for Pakistan. Arundhati Reddy will start with the new ball for India. Richa Ghosh is standing up to the stumps. Muneeba is on strike. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ..

Looking ahead - A challenging chase awaits Pakistan, and a lot will depend on how they begin. The surface has played on the slower side, on which India, with their varied bowling attack, will be confident enough of getting the job done. Either way, it promises to be an entertaining second half of the game, so stick around.

A quick word with Pakistan's head coach - Wahab Riaz says that they should have restricted India under 160 with the way we started, and might have given 10-15 runs extra at the end. Adds that a few dropped catches were where they lost the momentum, and the message was clear to just stick to the plans. Mentions that he is feeling confident of the team's chances in this chase, and they just need to play one ball at a time. Believes they can chase this with a couple of overs left.

Pakistan's strong start was undone late - After losing the toss, Pakistan were disciplined with the ball early on and were rewarded with a couple of wickets in the Powerplay. Put on the back foot, Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet Kaur absorbed the pressure before gradually settling into their innings. Mandhana was the more dominant of the two during their 91-run partnership and was handed reprieves along the way as Pakistan dropped her two catches. Having removed both set batters heading into the death overs, Pakistan had a genuine opportunity to limit the damage. However, Richa Ghosh came through for India with an aggressive cameo as Pakistan were made to pay for the slow over rate in the last two overs.

India get the desired finish - 38 runs off the last 2 overs have powered India to 170, and they will take it, given the kind of start they had to their innings. Pakistan started well but could not close out the innings they would have liked, and a stiff task awaits them with the bat.

The on-field decision is upheld! So 15 runs from the final over and India Women finish strongly at 170/6. A good length delivery on the leg stump line. Shreyanka premeditates and goes for a reverse scoop but misses, taking it on the front pad perhaps. The ball drops and rolls just beside the pitch, but the batters are alert to the situation to sneak in a run. Fatima goes up for the LBW appeal, but the umpire is unmoved, and Sana is quick to opt for a review, challenging the on-field decision. The UltraEdge shows the ball has hit Shreyanka on the gloves as there is a clear spike on it.

Any score over 160 is going to be a tough one to chase and with the current rate, and eight wickets in hand, that figure looks quite achievable.

Smriti again backs away to create room and loft it down the ground, but has barely any power behind the shot as she mistimes it off the toe end of the bat. Sails over mid off, where Aliya Riaz runs over her left shoulder and gets both hands stretched forward, but cannot get them to the ball. They cross. A huge let-off for Mandhana.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! It all started with fireworks for India as Shafali Verma struck a biggie on the first ball of the contest, but it has been all Pakistan since then as they've struck twice and are in a much better position than India after 6 overs. With just 38 runs on the board, having lost 2 of their top-three batters, Smriti Mandhana will be needed to build a steady partnership along with Harmanpreet Kaur. Pakistan Women will be hoping to break this partnership as soon as they can, as that will put India Women under immense pressure.

FOUR! Half a chance and it races away! Pitched fuller and on the off stump line. Smriti Mandhana brings her bat vertically down but cannot keep the straight drive along the ground. Chips it to the right of the bowler. It goes at a catchable height to Sana's right, who extends her right hand out on the follow-through. But the ball stays out of her reach and runs down the ground. The mid off fielder gives it a chase, but the ball wins the race.

Commentary.Commentary: Alright, done with the pre-match rituals. The anthems are proudly sung/chanted. It is time to get down to real business in Birmingham. The atmosphere at Edgbaston is absolutely electric, with a huge crowd turning up in support of both teams. It is a bit overcast out there, but nothing as threatening. Fatima Sana leads her ladies out as the players of Pakistan Women take their spots on the field. Out walk the two Indian openers - Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma. Shafali will face the first ball and it will be spin in the form of Sadia Iqbal to bowl the opening over. 3... 2... 1... and off we go...

Time for the national anthems - A huge cheer goes up from the crowd at Edgbaston as the giant flags are unveiled in the middle. The match officials make their way out. Out walk Harmanpreet Kaur and Fatima Sana, who lead their respective groups to get lined up for the anthems. It will be the national anthem of Pakistan first, followed by India's.

PITCH REPORT - Jatin Sapru notes that the same surface will be used for the entire tournament, and it has a good covering of dry grass. He adds that it will offer consistent bounce and carry, with the spinners coming into play as the game wears on. Veda Krishnamurthy notes there is dry grass on top, but it is rock hard underneath, so she reckons that the ball will come on nicely onto the bat. She points out that both sides have plenty of spin to call upon and feels the slower bowlers will be the ones to bring success here.
Pakistan Women (Playing XI) - Gull Feroza, Muneeba Ali (WK), Ayesha Zafar, Saira Jabeen, Aliya Riaz, Natalia Pervaiz, Fatima Sana (C), Rameen Shamim, Nashra Sundhu, Tasmia Rubab and Sadia Iqbal.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Bharti Fulmali, Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Arundhati Reddy, Shreyanka Patil, Sree Charani and Kranti Gaud.

The captain of Pakistan Women - Fatima Sana says that they would have batted first as well as it looks like a good batting wicket. On improvements, she says the team is doing well in both batting and bowling, but stresses that with a good bowling unit in place, they need to improve a little on their batting. On her fitness, she says the knee is good. And about the conditions, she feels it looks like a batting track, but with a good unit on both sides, it should be a good contest. When asked about the team combination, she reveals Saira Jabeen is in and will be playing her first World Cup match.

The Indian captain - Harmanpreet Kaur says they are going to bat first as it is a very good pitch to bat on and they'll be looking to put a good amount of runs on the board. On whether winning the ODI World Cup boosts their confidence, she says the whole team is excited and that the triumph has given them a lot of confidence, which they will look to carry forward. On their preparation, she says they have improved in several areas and stresses that they just need to get things right during the tournament. On team combination, she reveals Bharti Fulmali comes in for the game, noting that Yastika has been in good form but they decided to go with the former for this game. She also adds that they are going with three spinners and two medium pacers.

TOSS - Righto, it's time for the coin flip in this biggest rivalry. Both captains are out in the middle with Mel Jones leading the proceedings. Heads is the call from Fatima, but it lands as Tails. India Women have elected to BAT first.

Bangladesh hold nerves to win - Match 5 has ended, where Bangladesh Women have successfully launched their campaign with a thrilling 6-wicket victory over tournament debutants Netherlands Women. Chasing a target of 140, the Asian side held their nerves in the final overs to cross the finish line, thanks to a late innings blitz by Shorna Akter and Sharmin Akter.

Erasing recent stumbles on the big stage - Both teams arrive at Edgbaston searching for clinical consistency following shaky preparation periods. India suffered a 2-1 away series loss to England and split their official warm-up fixtures, defeating the West Indies but falling again to the English side. Pakistan's path has been even rockier. After a home win against Zimbabwe, they finished dead last in an Irish tri-series and dropped consecutive warm-up games to Sri Lanka and Scotland. With both teams needing to erase these recent setbacks, this opening match will be a pure test of mental fortitude under the intense global spotlight. Toss and team news to follow...

Death-over drama in Match 5 - The ICC Women's T20 World Cup Group A action is building massive momentum with a dramatic finish in Match 5, serving as the perfect prelude to the highly anticipated India vs Pakistan showdown. The Netherlands Women have set a competitive target of 140 runs, and the chase hangs in absolute balance as Bangladesh Women require 19 runs from the final 18 balls. Bangladesh currently stands at 121 for 4 after 17 overs, with the set batting pair of Shorna Akter and Sharmin Akhter holding the key to a crucial victory. Both teams are fighting hard in the death overs, providing a high-octane warm-up for fans waiting for the ultimate Asian rivalry next on the schedule.

Pakistan aiming to shatter the underdog label - Pakistan enter the tournament eager to spring a massive early surprise under the fresh leadership of captain Fatima Sana. Pakistan has a reputation for playing spoilers when underestimated. The squad raised eyebrows close to the tournament by omitting experienced top-order batter Sidra Amin, signalling a tactical shift toward dynamic youth. Explosive keeper-opener Muneeba Ali anchors the top order, with power hitters like Aliya Riaz, the veteran Iram Javed, and skipper Fatima providing late-innings firepower. Pakistan’s strategy will rely on disrupting India's star-studded batting rhythm right from the first ball.

India's hunt for another title - Despite establishing themselves as a modern powerhouse in women’s cricket, India enter the 2026 edition desperate to capture their maiden T20 World Cup trophy. The squad is still fueled by the sting of the 2024 tournament, where they failed to reach the semi-finals after finishing third in their group. Leading the charge is the iconic Harmanpreet Kaur. India boast a terrifyingly explosive batting order featuring Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, and Jemimah Rodrigues. Their lineup is further bolstered by elite all-rounders Deepti Sharma and Shreyanka Patil, alongside returning keeper-batter Yastika Bhatia, giving India enviable tactical depth.

Cricket's greatest rivalry - Hello and welcome everyone. India Women and Pakistan Women are set to reignite one of international sport's most passionate rivalries at Edgbaston, Birmingham, in a contest that carries immense psychological weight far beyond the two tournament points on offer. With global powerhouses Australia and South Africa looming in the same group, neither side can afford a sluggish start.
... MATCHDAY ...

Biggest battle locked and loaded - Call it the mother of all rivalries, or one of the biggest and fiercest of all clashes, in any sport for that matter, it all comes down to this particular match in every ICC tournament when the cricketing landscape reaches a competitive peak. It’s the arch-rivals of the subcontinent going hammer and tongs against each other. Arguably, the biggest game of Group A sees India Women taking on Pakistan Women, and the battlefield is Edgbaston, Birmingham, all ready to add another glorious chapter to its already storied history.  The tournament is just slowly igniting, but we’ve had some gripping moments in the tournament already, with the highest Women's T20 World Cup score notched up in the curtain raiser. Drawn into a group alongside marquee sides like Australia and South Africa, who can prove too hot to handle on their day, both these sides know that a strong start to their campaign will put them a mile ahead. Form holds the key - India's batting lineup runs deep, but right now one name stands above the rest. Captain Harmanpreet Kaur is in red-hot form, India's leading run scorer in T20Is in 2026 with an average of 48.5 that towers above the rest of the order. Shafali Verma and Jemimah Rodrigues sit just behind her on that list. Smriti Mandhana, on the other hand, has hit a rare rough patch, managing just 40 runs in the recent series against England. But zoom out, and the picture changes completely. Since the last T20 World Cup, she has piled up 765 runs, including a century and six fifties, making her India's highest run scorer in that period by a distance. The real worry lies further down. Richa Ghosh, usually India's finisher with bat in hand, has gone through her last eight innings without crossing single digits in five of those, the dip spanning across two full series. Yastika Bhatia waits in the wings as the alternative, but India can't afford too much experimentation and need someone in that finisher's role to find form, and fast. Blend of youth and experience with the ball - India's bowling attack might just be their trump card heading into this tournament. Up front, Renuka Singh Thakur brings the kind of new ball swing that can rattle any top order, and she won't be working alone, with a pace unit behind her that adds both depth and variety. Where India really stand out, though, is spin. Four specialist options give the team plenty of room to mix and match depending on conditions, and Sree Charani has been the pick of them in 2026, India's leading wicket taker for the year so far in T20Is. Then there's the experience factor. Deepti Sharma, playing her fifth T20 World Cup, is the highest wicket taker among the current squad in the tournament's history, behind only Poonam Yadav. Radha Yadav, also in her fifth World Cup, brings over 100 wickets in the format alongside her. Together, these two give India a spin core built on years of big-match experience. Throw in the rising Shreyanka Patil, already making big leaps despite her young career, and India suddenly look like a side with both a proven core and exciting depth coming through. Walking into a big transition - Pakistan arrive at this World Cup in the middle of a serious changing of the guard. The PCB has handed the captaincy to young allrounder Fatima Sana, and in the same breath, dropped former skipper and veteran campaigner Nida Dar from the squad entirely. It's a bold call that strips the side of its most experienced head and pushes a younger core straight into the deep end. So far, Fatima Sana has worn the extra responsibility well. She is Pakistan's leading run scorer in T20Is this year, averaging an insane 74.5 with close to 300 runs already banked. Along the way, she also smashed the fastest fifty in women's T20I history, off just 15 balls, at a strike rate north of 200. Her captaincy reign began on a high note, with Pakistan sweeping Zimbabwe 3-0 in both the ODI and T20I series at home in May. Time to prove under pressure - Pakistan's middle order lacks genuine power hitters, which puts a lot of pressure on opener Muneeba Ali and senior allrounder Aliya Riaz to set the tone. Early wickets tend to drag their scoring rate down fast, often leaving the bowlers chasing a total that's already short of par. For things to click, the likes of Gull Feroza, Eyman Fatima and Natalia Pervaiz will need to step up and deliver when it matters most. On the bowling front, there's cautious optimism around Diana Baig, Pakistan's premier seamer, who is hoping to get through a full tournament after injury cut short her 2024 campaign. She has played just three T20Is since then, which means a big chunk of the pace bowling load will fall on Fatima Sana. The new captain is already Pakistan's second-highest wicket taker in T20Is this year, trailing only Sadia Iqbal, so she'll be juggling runs, wickets and leadership all at once. Team form (Last 5 completed Women’s T20Is, recent first) - IND-W - LLWLW | PAK-W - LLWWW. What to expect? Edgbaston has a reputation for serving up high-scoring contests, and big chases are nothing new here either. The tournament opener at this venue saw England post a massive 219 against Sri Lanka. There was some movement for the new ball early on, but as the innings wore on, the pitch settled down and looked good for batting. With overcast conditions expected in Birmingham on Sunday, though, the bowlers could well have a say in this one. History, by and large, favours India in this rivalry. The Women in Blue lead the overall T20I head-to-head 13-3, and Pakistan's last win over India in the format came all the way back at the 2022 Asia Cup. Even in World Cup meetings specifically, Pakistan have managed just two wins from eight, with both coming in the 2012 and 2016 editions. Records aside, this is a World Cup clash between two proud nations, desperate to find their feet again, and that alone should make for box office viewing.
